angebot.name: Quoting Coworker
angebot.subject: Re: Inquiry 50 hydraulic valves — quote prepared
angebot.body1: Good morning. The inquiry from Bauer Landtechnik came in. I've reviewed it, cross-checked with our ERP, and prepared the quote.
angebot.body2: Material and effort calculated based on the last 6 orders with Bauer. Terms: existing customer, delivery in 4 weeks — fits your standard margin.
angebot.closing: Reply 'approve' and I'll send the quote out. Or adjust the price first.
angebot.footer: Quote draft saved in your CRM · History: 6 orders

rezeption.name: Reception Coworker
rezeption.subject: Call handled — Müller GmbH, callback requested
rezeption.body1: Call from Ms. Schmidt, Müller GmbH, at 09:42 came in. I took the call, captured all details, and classified the request.
rezeption.body2: It's about a delivery delay on order #4712. Ms. Schmidt requests a callback by 14:00. I've blocked your calendar and opened the order in our ERP.
rezeption.closing: Should I send a status update mail to Müller GmbH first? Reply 'yes' or 'no'.
rezeption.footer: Calls today: 7 · Mails: 12 · Status: all handled

monitoring.name: Monitoring Coworker
monitoring.subject: Proactive alert — Server SRV-04 showing anomalies
monitoring.body1: Just noticed overnight: Server SRV-04 has shown unusual behavior since 03:14 — CPU load constantly above 85%, normally under 30%. I've analyzed your logs.
monitoring.body2: Cause: a cron job from the last deployment is running in an infinite loop. Compared historically, the pattern is identical to the incident on March 18. Back then, you stopped the job manually.
monitoring.closing: I can stop the cron job and notify the team automatically. Should I? Otherwise I'll keep watching and report at 09:00.

disposition.name: Dispatching Coworker
disposition.subject: Tour planning Wednesday — 3 new orders slotted in
disposition.body1: Three new orders came in today. I've slotted them into the existing Wednesday tour, with minimal detour and without breaking time windows.
disposition.body2: Order optimized: order #4801 (Schmitt) before #4789 (Becker) — saves 42 km and keeps the 10–12 delivery window for Becker. Driver Müller is assigned.
disposition.closing: Tour plan updated, driver app synced. Only reply if you want changes.
disposition.footer: 3 orders assigned · 0 time-window violations · Resources: optimal

leadResearch.name: Lead Research Coworker
leadResearch.subject: Lead research machinery DACH — 12 matches
leadResearch.body1: Overnight I screened your three target verticals — machinery, special machinery, tool building — against your filter (50–250 employees, DACH).
leadResearch.body2: 12 qualified companies identified. Per lead: company profile, decision makers, current tech stack, pain points from job postings and LinkedIn activity, outreach hook. Full report attached.
leadResearch.closing: Reply with a lead number and I'll draft a personalized outreach email for that lead.
leadResearch.footer: Data as of 2026-05-07 · Full report attached

hohenloher.problem: Manually checking dimensions and DIN standards on technical drawings costs engineers hours — and errors slip through.
hohenloher.solution: Coworker reviews incoming technical drawings for dimensional consistency and DIN compliance, flags deviations, documents an audit trail.
hohenloher.outcome: Engineers review results instead of manually checking.

maschinenbauer.problem: Technicians receive schematics and need to compile information from multiple documents before they can even start work.
maschinenbauer.solution: Coworker reads schematics, identifies relevant components, prepares a structured info briefing for the technician — including data sheets and prior data.
maschinenbauer.outcome: Technicians start with full context instead of research.

rstDatentechnik.problem: Outages get detected too late, reports handled too late, customers informed too late. Classic SME support bottleneck.
rstDatentechnik.solution: Coworker monitors systems proactively, takes incident reports, classifies by severity, coordinates with technicians, keeps customers informed.
rstDatentechnik.outcome: Faster response, fewer escalations, support team relieved.

SecurityArchitecture.label: Security & Architecture
SecurityArchitecture.headline: AI Coworker. Secure, controlled, productive.
SecurityArchitecture.subline: Your digital coworker for mid-market companies. Communicates, researches, and completes tasks. With built-in security architecture.
SecurityArchitecture.networkDesc: No unrestricted internet access. Only explicitly whitelisted services are reachable. Everything else is blocked.
SecurityArchitecture.permissionsDesc: Every action runs with minimum required privileges. Based on trigger, task, and whether a human or automation is acting.
SecurityArchitecture.emailDesc: Manipulative content is not interpreted as instructions. Protected against prompt injection attacks via email.
SecurityArchitecture.toolsDesc: Only assigned tools per task. Every action is traceable. No uncontrolled access.
SecurityArchitecture.benefitDesc: Your team is relieved, routine processes run faster — without compromising on security. The coworker operates within clearly defined boundaries, always under your team's control.
SecurityArchitecture.scope_userBased: User-Based: Permissions by trigger (customer vs. employee)
SecurityArchitecture.scope_automationBased: Automation-Based: Tighter permissions for autonomous agents
SecurityArchitecture.scope_fileBased: File-Based: Access restricted at file system level
SecurityArchitecture.memoryVector: Vector-PostgreSQL for session content, retrievable via vector search
SecurityArchitecture.memoryContext: Context managed via orchestrator and task comments
SecurityArchitecture.footnote: Security is not a feature — it's an architectural principle.
